title: Korea Stock Market Today, Oct 27, 2026: KOSPI +3.09%, KOSDAQ +2.29% as Anthropic IPO Hopes Lift Chip Stocks
content:
KOSPI closed at 5,638.34, up 3.09%, and KOSDAQ closed at 743.83, up 2.29%, as hopes around Anthropic's IPO filing lifted chip stocks and a buy-side sidecar was triggered on KOSPI during the session. Individual themes moved on their own news: substrate and PCB makers, test and back-end equipment names, newly listed stocks led by Melcon's upper-limit move, Hyundai Motor Group's Atlas supply chain, cybersecurity stocks and energy storage (ESS) names.

1. Anthropic IPO hopes — Korean stocks rebound, chip stocks strengthen

U.S. tech and chip stocks rebounded on news that U.S. AI company Anthropic filed for an initial public offering with the Securities and Exchange Commission. The Nasdaq rose 0.82% and the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index rose 2.82%, reviving expectations for AI industry growth, and lower oil prices also helped sentiment. Korean markets rebounded strongly, led by large chip stocks. Early in the session KOSPI recovered the 5,700 level and was up more than 4%, triggering a buy-side sidecar, and KOSDAQ was up more than 3%. KOSPI ultimately closed at 5,638.34 (+3.09%) and KOSDAQ at 743.83 (+2.29%). SK hynix and Samsung Electronics led the gains, with SK Square, SK Telecom and Samsung Electro-Mechanics also strong. The Fed meeting and major big tech earnings this week mean it remains to be seen whether the rebound lasts.

2. Chip stocks — buying spreads to substrate, PCB, test and back-end names

As AI investment sentiment recovered, buying spread beyond large chip stocks to substrate and PCB makers and to test and back-end equipment makers, on expectations of demand for parts and inspection equipment as AI servers and high-performance chips grow. Names in focus: large chip stocks SK hynix, Samsung Electronics, SK Square, SK Telecom and Samsung Electro-Mechanics; substrate and PCB makers Simmtech, TLB, Korea Circuit, Daeduck Electronics, ISU Petasys and Gigavis; test, back-end and inspection names Exicon, TFE, Micro Contact Solution, Koh Young, Genesem, Neosem and TSE; and memory-related names Hanyang Digitech, Dreamtech and Uniquest.

3. Rotation among newly listed stocks — Melcon hits its upper limit

As buying flowed into the chip sector, rotation continued among newly listed stocks. Melcon, which develops and supplies ultra-precise environmental control equipment for semiconductor photo processes, hit its upper limit. Buying also came into Global Technology, Haechitec, Neosapience, MS Bio and Elice, with sector strength and individual supply and demand driving different names.

4. Hyundai Motor Group's Atlas supply chain — camera and parts stocks in focus

News that Korean battery and camera suppliers take part in Hyundai Motor Group's Atlas humanoid robot supply chain drew attention. According to reports, Samsung SDI and LG Energy Solution supply batteries, and Hyundai Mobis, Namuga, MCNEX and Camsys take part in cameras. Camsys, Namuga, MCNEX and BH were in focus. Expectations for demand for actuators, Atlas's core drive parts, also lifted names including AxVis, which hit its upper limit, and Woorim PTS. Being included in the theme does not confirm that each company directly supplies Atlas.

5. Cybersecurity stocks — PHP vulnerability and financial-sector hacking worries

Buying came into cybersecurity stocks after a security vulnerability was reported in PHP, widely used in website development, and as worries about hacking and personal data leaks at financial firms continued. Expectations rose for stronger security and demand for related solutions. AhnLab, Sands Lab, S2W, Raon Secure, Aton and Xgate were in focus. Gains and backgrounds differ by stock, and theme-driven buying also played a role.

6. ESS stocks — energy storage demand and expansion hopes

Interest in energy storage system (ESS) stocks continued as AI data center growth raised power demand and the need for stable supply. In Korea, a 2026 central contract market tender for 1,180 MW of ESS capacity is being pursued, a sign of market expansion, and battery makers' ESS expansion could serve as a medium- to long-term investment theme. Sangsin EDP, Shinheung SEC and HT Robotics were in focus.

Quick FAQ

How did KOSPI and KOSDAQ close on Oct 27?
KOSPI rose 3.09% to 5,638.34 and KOSDAQ rose 2.29% to 743.83. A buy-side sidecar was triggered on KOSPI during the session.

Why did Korean stocks rebound?
U.S. tech and chip stocks rose after Anthropic filed for an IPO with the SEC (Nasdaq +0.82%, Philadelphia Semiconductor Index +2.82%), and lower oil prices also helped sentiment.

Do all Atlas-related stocks directly supply the robot?
No. Being included in the theme does not confirm that each company directly supplies Atlas.
